concepts.name: Extent of reaction
concepts.statement: The single variable ξ that measures how far a reaction has run: each amount changes as n_i = n_{i,0} − ν_iξ for a reactant and n_{i,0} + ν_iξ for a product, so ξ is in moles. Starting from ν moles of the limiting reactant it runs from 0 to 1 at completion, and a reaction that reaches equilibrium stops at ξ_eq.

concepts.name: Measuring the extent of reaction
concepts.statement: Following a quantity q that depends linearly on the extent, q(ξ) = aξ + b (an absorbance, a conductivity, a mass, a heat), gives ξ = (q − q₀)/(q₁ − q₀) from its values at the start and at completion; where those cannot be observed, a and b are fitted to the data.

concepts.name: Reaction Gibbs energy
concepts.statement: At constant T and P, writing every dn_i as ±ν_i dξ turns dG = Σμ_i dn_i into a single slope: Δ_rG = (∂G/∂ξ)_{T,P} = Σν_iμ_i over products minus reactants, the change in G per mole of reaction as written at a fixed composition, in J/mol.

concepts.name: Equilibrium at the minimum of the Gibbs energy
concepts.statement: At constant T and P a reaction moves down the curve of G against ξ: the slope Δ_rG is negative on one side of the minimum and positive on the other, so the reaction runs toward the minimum from either side and stops where (∂G/∂ξ)_{T,P} = Δ_rG = 0. For A ⇌ B this is where μ_A = μ_B.

concepts.name: Standard reaction Gibbs energy
terms: standard Gibbs free energy of reaction
concepts.statement: The reaction Gibbs energy with every species in its standard state, Δ_rG° = Σν_iμ_i° over products minus reactants: a property of the reaction looked up in tables, whose value depends on the standard pressures chosen.

concepts.name: Reaction quotient
concepts.statement: The product of the species' relative pressures (or concentrations, or activities), each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient, products over reactants: Q = (P_Y/P°)^{ν_Y}(P_Z/P°)^{ν_Z}/((P_A/P°)^{ν_A}(P_B/P°)^{ν_B}). The standard pressures make Q dimensionless; Q_P, written without them, equals Q in magnitude.

concepts.name: Reaction Gibbs energy from the reaction quotient
concepts.statement: For ideal gases μ_i = μ_i° + RT ln(P_i/P_i°), so the reaction Gibbs energy splits into its standard value and a composition term: Δ_rG = Δ_rG° + RT ln Q. Δ_rG describes the reaction at its actual pressures, Δ_rG° at standard conditions.

concepts.name: Equilibrium constant
concepts.statement: The value K that the reaction quotient takes at equilibrium, where Δ_rG = 0: for gases the quotient of the equilibrium partial pressures, K = P_{eq,Y}^{ν_Y}P_{eq,Z}^{ν_Z}/(P_{eq,A}^{ν_A}P_{eq,B}^{ν_B}).

concepts.name: Equilibrium constant from the standard reaction Gibbs energy
concepts.statement: Setting Δ_rG = Δ_rG° + RT ln K = 0 at equilibrium gives Δ_rG° = −RT ln K, so K = e^{−Δ_rG°/RT}. Δ_rG° is not zero, because the standard state is in general not an equilibrium state.

concepts.name: The equilibrium constant depends on temperature only
concepts.statement: For a reaction of ideal gases K depends only on T, not on the total pressure, because Δ_rG° refers to fixed standard pressures. In non-ideal gases and solutions K can shift a little with pressure or ionic strength through the fugacity or activity coefficients.

concepts.name: van 't Hoff equation
concepts.statement: Putting ln K = −Δ_rG°/RT into the Gibbs–Helmholtz equation gives (∂ln K/∂T)_P = Δ_rH°/RT²: K rises with temperature for an endothermic reaction and falls for an exothermic one.

concepts.name: Integrated van 't Hoff equation
concepts.statement: With Δ_rH° taken as independent of temperature, integrating the van 't Hoff equation gives ln[K(T₂)/K(T₁)] = −(Δ_rH°/R)(1/T₂ − 1/T₁), which carries K from one temperature to another; heat-capacity data correct it where more precision is needed.

concepts.name: Extent of a gas dissociation against pressure
concepts.statement: For A ⇌ B + C starting from one mole of A, Dalton's law gives partial pressures (1 − ξ)P/(1 + ξ) and ξP/(1 + ξ), so K = Pξ_eq²/(1 − ξ_eq²): at fixed K, raising the total pressure P lowers ξ_eq.

concepts.name: Le Chatelier's principle
concepts.statement: When the total pressure of a gas reaction is changed, K stays the same but the equilibrium extent shifts in response, toward the side with fewer molecules on compression.

concepts.name: Molarity
concepts.statement: The molar amount per unit volume, c = n/V; for an ideal gas the gas law hides it as P = cRT, so c = P/RT.

concepts.name: Equilibrium constant in concentrations
concepts.statement: Written in equilibrium molarities, K = c_{eq,Y}^{ν_Y}c_{eq,Z}^{ν_Z}/(c_{eq,A}^{ν_A}c_{eq,B}^{ν_B}); substituting c = P/RT leaves a factor of RT to the power g = ν_Y + ν_Z − ν_A − ν_B, which is absorbed into Δ_rG°, now referred to a standard state of 1 mol/L of each species.

concepts.name: Reaction Gibbs energy from enthalpy and entropy
concepts.statement: Substituting μ_i = H_i − TS_i into Δ_rG = Σν_iμ_i gives Δ_rG = Δ_rH − TΔ_rS, and with every species in its standard state Δ_rG° = Δ_rH° − TΔ_rS°, where Δ_rS° = Σν_iS_i°.

concepts.name: Standard Gibbs energy of formation
terms: standard molar Gibbs energy of formation
concepts.statement: The standard molar reaction Gibbs energy of a substance's formation reaction, Δ_fG° = Δ_fH° − TΣν_iS_i°, evaluated from its enthalpy of formation and the standard molar entropies of the reactants and product; tabulated for substances and ions, often at 298.15 K.

concepts.name: Reaction Gibbs energy from Gibbs energies of formation
concepts.statement: As in Hess's law, Δ_rG° = Σν_iΔ_fG°(i) over the reactants and products, so tabulated Gibbs energies of formation give Δ_rG° and then K; since Δ_fH° comes from calorimetry and S° from heat capacities, K can be found from calorimetry alone.

concepts.name: Reference values for aqueous ions
concepts.statement: Since no formation reaction can be written for a single ion, the values of S_m° and Δ_fG° for ions in aqueous solution are referred to H⁺(aq), for which S_m° = 0, Δ_fH° = 0 and Δ_fG° = 0 at all temperatures; some ions therefore have negative standard molar entropies.

concepts.name: Gibbs energy of formation of an ion
concepts.statement: From a hypothetical reaction that forms the ion from the elements with H⁺(aq) and H₂(g), Δ_fG°(M^{z+}) = Δ_fH°(M^{z+}) − T[S_m°(M^{z+}) − Σ S_i°(elements) + (z₊/2)S_m°(H₂)], and for an anion the same with −|z₋/2|S_m°(H₂).

concepts.name: Exergonic and endergonic reactions
concepts.statement: A reaction with Δ_rG < 0 is exergonic and runs forward spontaneously; one with Δ_rG > 0 is endergonic and runs in reverse; at Δ_rG = 0 it is at equilibrium.

concepts.name: Equilibrium position
concepts.statement: The extent ξ_eq at the minimum of G against ξ, toward which a reaction moves spontaneously from either side.

concepts.name: Mixing puts the minimum inside the reaction
concepts.statement: For A ⇌ B between ideal gases, G against ξ is the straight line of the pure species' standard Gibbs energies plus the Gibbs energy of mixing, nRT(χ_A ln χ_A + χ_B ln χ_B), which is lowest at half and half; with Δ_rG° = 0 the minimum is at χ_A = χ_B = 0.5, and Δ_rG° moves it toward the side of lower standard Gibbs energy, so the minimum always lies between pure reactant and pure product.

concepts.name: Q against K decides the direction
concepts.statement: Subtracting 0 = Δ_rG° + RT ln K from Δ_rG = Δ_rG° + RT ln Q gives Δ_rG = RT ln(Q/K): if Q < K the reaction shifts right to make products, if Q > K it shifts left, and Q changes until Q = K.

concepts.name: The sign of Δ_rG, not Δ_rG°, decides spontaneity
concepts.statement: Δ_rG° describes the idealised standard state (1 bar of each gas, 1 M in solution, unmixed), which is not the real reaction mixture; whether a reaction runs forward depends on the sign of Δ_rG = Δ_rG° + RT ln Q at the actual composition, which reaches zero, with Q = K, at equilibrium.

concepts.name: Linear van 't Hoff plot
concepts.statement: With Δ_rG° = Δ_rH° − TΔ_rS°, K = e^{−Δ_rH°/RT}e^{Δ_rS°/R}, so ln K = −(Δ_rH°/R)(1/T) + Δ_rS°/R: a plot of ln K against 1/T is a line of slope −Δ_rH°/R and intercept Δ_rS°/R, which gives both from equilibrium data without calorimetry, as long as they depend only weakly on T.

concepts.name: Chemical potential from the molecular partition function
concepts.statement: With A = −k_BT ln(q_i^{N_i}/N_i!) and Stirling's approximation, μ_i = (∂A/∂N_i)_{T,V} = −k_BT ln(q_i/N_i) for a species of independent, indistinguishable molecules.

concepts.name: Equilibrium at the minimum of the Helmholtz energy
concepts.statement: At fixed T and V, with dN_j = ν_j dλ (ν_j positive for products, negative for reactants), dA = Σμ_jν_j dλ, and equilibrium is where (∂A/∂λ)_{T,V} = 0, that is Σν_jμ_j = 0.

concepts.name: Equilibrium constant from partition functions
concepts.statement: Putting μ_j = −k_BT ln(q_j/N_j) into Σν_jμ_j = 0 and dividing by the volume gives K_c = ρ_C^{ν_C}ρ_D^{ν_D}/(ρ_A^{ν_A}ρ_B^{ν_B}) = (q_C/V)^{ν_C}(q_D/V)^{ν_D}/((q_A/V)^{ν_A}(q_B/V)^{ν_B}): the molecular partition functions of the species give the equilibrium constant.

concepts.name: Computing an equilibrium constant from molecular data
concepts.statement: Write each q/V as the product of translational, rotational, vibrational and electronic factors, (2πmk_BT/h²)^{3/2} · T/(σΘ_r) · 1/(1 − e^{−Θ_ν/T}) · g₁e^{D₀/RT}, evaluate them per species from the masses, Θ_r, Θ_ν and D₀, and combine them as the equilibrium constant's quotient.

concepts.name: Tabulated thermochemical data
concepts.statement: Because accurate partition functions of real molecules need complex corrections, partition functions and thermodynamic properties are tabulated, as in the JANAF tables: C_P, S°, G° and H° relative to H°(298.15 K), Δ_fH°, Δ_fG° and log K_f against temperature, combining experiment with theory.

concepts.name: Fugacity coefficient from the compression factor
concepts.statement: Since (∂μ/∂p)_T = V = RT(∂ln f/∂p)_T, the fugacity obeys (∂ln f/∂p)_T = Z/p, and with f = γp integrating from 0, where every gas is ideal and γ = 1, gives ln γ = ∫₀^p (Z − 1)/p dp.

concepts.name: Thermodynamic equilibrium constant in activities
concepts.statement: With μ_i = μ_i° + RT ln a_i the same steps give K in equilibrium activities, K = a_{eq,Y}^{ν_Y}a_{eq,Z}^{ν_Z}/(a_{eq,A}^{ν_A}a_{eq,B}^{ν_B}); writing a_i = γ_ic_i/c_i° splits it as K = K_γK_c/K_{c°}, where K_{c°} is unity and only cancels dimensions and K_γ is unity only for an ideal solution.

concepts.name: Activity of a pure condensed phase under pressure
concepts.statement: For a pure solid or liquid with its standard state at 1 bar, dμ = RT d ln a = V̄ dP with a small, nearly constant molar volume, so ln a' = (P' − 1)V̄/RT: the activity stays close to one (graphite's is about 1.01 at 100 bar), and is taken as unity in reactions.

concepts.name: Equilibrium among pure condensed phases
concepts.statement: If every species is a pure condensed phase, all activities are one, Q = 1 and Δ_rG = Δ_rG°, so equilibrium is possible only at the single temperature T = Δ_rH°/Δ_rS° (a melting point, for example); at any other temperature the process goes to completion. Equilibrium over a range of temperatures needs a species whose activity depends on composition, such as a solute or a gas.

concepts.name: Correcting an ionic equilibrium for activities by iteration
concepts.statement: Solve the equilibrium first as ideal, use the concentrations to find the ionic strength and γ± from an extended Debye–Hückel equation, divide K by the activity-coefficient factor, solve again, and repeat until the concentration no longer changes: for 0.1 mol/L acetic acid x moves from 1.31 to about 1.37 × 10⁻³ mol/L.

concepts.name: Non-ideality raises the solubility of a sparingly soluble salt
concepts.statement: In a solubility product K = γ±³[Ba²⁺][F⁻]² the activity coefficients fall below one as the dissolved ions raise the ionic strength, so the solubility rises above the ideal estimate (for BaF₂ from 7.52 × 10⁻³ to about 0.011 mol/L), and other solutes, adding to the ionic strength, raise it further.
